newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels declare unilateral ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels declare unilateral ceasefire.

text.p: Rebels in eastern Zaire declared a unilateral ceasefire on Thursday and called on the international community to push Zaire's government to negotiate.
"Because of much pressure from abroad we have stopped (the war)," Laurent Kabila, leader of the Alliance of Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire, told Reuters.
But Kabila warned in an interview:
"This (war) can continue if there is not a clear indication from the international community and the gang in power in Kinshasa to say they are willing to surrender or to start negotiations."
Kabila said advancing rebel forces had stopped short of the towns of Walikale, where he said the Zairean army was being reinforced, and Bunia.
The rebels control the main eastern towns of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira after a two-month campaign against the ragged Zairean army.
